subject: Dedicated reservation: preemptible pool carveout & preemption addendum request
messages:
From: Ava Murray <ava.murray@northbridge.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Procurement <procurement@northbridge.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation question — preemptible pool behavior and addendum

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are finalizing the internal recommendation for reserved GPU capacity (reserve + burst) but Procurement flagged preemption behavior for any preemptible/spot-like pools that could share capacity in our reserved SKU. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood guarantee a throughput floor (percent of committed p90 tokens/sec) during business hours (M-F 08:00–18:00 PST) for routes we mark as critical?
2) If preemption is possible, can we get a contract addendum that outlines carveouts (time-sliced / tenant isolation) and a crediting scheme when the throughput floor is missed?

We attached a short matrix of traffic patterns and the places we expect deterministic throughput (preemption_matrix.xlsx). Ideally we’d like a draft of the addendum to circulate to Legal/Procurement — is that something you can provide or we should pull together?

Prefer a short call if helpful; otherwise please reply with proposed language/limits.

Appreciate it,
Ava Murray
Head of Platform Ops
Northbridge AI

Attachments: preemption_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with route definitions and critical windows)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ava Murray <ava.murray@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation question — preemptible pool behavior and addendum

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear matrix, and for surfacing this early. We can absolutely put forward a contract addendum that defines a deterministic throughput floor for routes you mark as critical. High-level options we typically propose (we can redline to match Northbridge wording):

- Time-sliced carveout: guarantee X% of committed throughput for specified routes during defined business hours (e.g., M-F 08:00–18:00 PST).
- Soft-isolation: dedicate a fraction of reserved pool capacity to critical routes with preemption blocked within the carveout window.
- Credit schedule: monthly credits for any hour where throughput floor < agreed threshold, capped per month.

Operational caveats: the flooring can be achieved by routing + soft isolation rather than physically separate hardware in most cases, but that depends on your concurrency patterns. Based on the matrix: 90–95% floor looks reasonable for steady-state critical routes; for bursting patterns we recommend a lower guaranteed floor with explicit escalation windows.

I’ve attached a draft addendum (reserved_capacity_addendum_draft.pdf) with a suggested 95% floor during the business hours you specified and a credit formula (hourly credit = 1/720 * committed monthly fee * breach_hours capped at 10% monthly). Please review and let me know which of the three options you prefer.

If this matches what Procurement needs, I can loop Legal and send a redline next week. Ben / Markus — please advise if the 95% floor + credit cap approach is acceptable from our risk/cost side.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reserved_capacity_addendum_draft.pdf (draft addendum — redline-ready)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation question — preemptible pool behavior and addendum

Eve / Markus —

Quick internal note after looking at the draft and the attached matrix: I support offering a time-sliced carveout for the routes Northbridge marks critical, but recommend the following changes before we send to Legal/Procurement:

- Limit hard no-preemption guarantee to routes that are pinned to the reserve pool and that maintain a steady CPU/GPU utilization profile. For highly spiky routes (they flagged a few), offer a lower guaranteed floor (e.g., 70%) and a faster escalation SLO.
- Convert the crediting formula to a sliding scale based on magnitude of shortfall (e.g., 70–80% shortfall = 0.25x hourly rate, 80–90% = 0.5x, <70% = 1x) — this helps bound our downside.
- Cap cumulative credits at 2x the monthly committed spend.
- Add an operational playbook clause: customer must provide final route tagging, a 30-day validation run, and a single 90-day trial period for any carveout.

I attached a short preemption_matrix.xlsx with suggested thresholds and an example calculation. If we’re aligned, I think Legal will be comfortable moving quickly on a redline.

Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: preemption_matrix.xlsx (internal suggested thresholds and credit table)

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation question — preemptible pool behavior and addendum

All —

Read both the draft and Ben’s thresholds. High-level decision: greenlight proposing a commercial addendum to Northbridge given strategic value and likely expansion upside, with these constraints:

- Approve time-sliced carveout for M-F 08:00–18:00 PST for routes Northbridge marks critical. Start with a 90-day trial window.
- Use Ben’s sliding credit scale and cap cumulative credits at 2x monthly committed spend.
- For highly spiky routes, offer a reduced committed floor (70%) and require a 30-day validation run before the carveout becomes active.
- Legal should own final redline; Sales to own sign-off with Procurement. Evelyn — please send the redline to Ava and procurement with Ben in copy and CC Legal (legal@redwood.com). Call out the operational playbook and the trial period in the first paragraph.

I’ll monitor — if Northbridge pushes for lower credit caps we’ll escalate. Good work.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
